READABILITY.evidence: Function names are mostly clear (renderAfterSaleList, submitRefundModal, handleConfirmReturnUI). But the 2376-line file has almost no comments on refund or stats logic, and uses short names like `o`, `r`, `v`, `l` in business loops (`state.orders.forEach(o => ... o.refunds.forEach(r => ...`).

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: One new 2376-line file, so capped at accept. renderAnalyticsUI recalculates grossPaid/refunded per SKU itself instead of using getStats, and refund-quantity counting is repeated in the modal. UI builds large HTML strings inline.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Hidden test test_cart_rejects_illegal_quantity failed, so some illegal quantities get through. Refund modal uses parseInt(input.value) with no check beyond `qty > 0`. Import does return an error, but coupon thresholds are hard-coded magic values in the HTML options.

C9-01-CASE1.evidence: Submitting an after-sale request (submitRefundModal), confirming a return into stock (handleConfirmReturnUI calls confirmReturn directly) and importing (handleImportFromTextarea) all run without a confirm step. Feedback is plain alert(); the coupon select does not explain the stacking rule.

C9-01-CASE2.evidence: UI handlers call the same functions as the API (requestAfterSale, confirmReturn, getStats), but the analytics view recalculates units separately. Money appears to be float yuan (`refund.amount.toFixed(2)`), not integer cents. Hidden test test_seed_products_and_orders failed.
